title.narrative: Unlocking Adaptation Finance for Smallholders Agribusiness in Ethiopia

description.narrative:
Support to Technoserve to integrate up to 20,000 small scale farmers into the seed-oil value chain of Semanu in Ethiopia.
Impact: Increased climate resilience and sustainable income growth for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia through inclusive agribusiness models and innovative access to inputs and financing.
Outcomes: 13,000 households with sustainable income increases; at least 8,000 smallholder farmers with access to financing; strengthened direct procurement for oilseed crops (sunflower, soybean, rapeseed); enhanced resilience to climate and market risks.
Outputs: Expanded advisory/extension services across multiple climate zones; seed multiplication and distribution of resilient varieties (incl securing local seeds); structures for input financing with financial partners; knowledge products and systematic monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL).
Main Activities: Advisory services and field follow-up; seed production and distribution; development of financing solutions with financial service providers; partnership development (including weather and insurance services); learning and policy work; program management and reporting.
Geography and Target Group: Smallholder farmers in Ethiopia within oilseed value chains; collaboration with Samanu (a Norfund-invested company).
Duration: 36 months (2025–2028). TechnoServe’s inclusive investment team brings deep expertise building gender sensitive frameworks, particularly the business case and technical solutions for agribusinesses to develop gender inclusive supply chains . The project leverages TechnoServe’s existing toolkit on promoting gender responsive business practices to drive gender quality and inclusion. The opportunities identified with Samanu cover the inclusion of women farmers in training and supply chain activities. They will also seek to refine the farmer recruitment strategy to increase women’s participation.
